candidates.exact_span: Select only those Elements and Sections which apply to your sludge reuse or disposal practice.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Elements and Sections are deemed applicable determines which numeric limits, monitoring requirements, and evidence expectations are in scope; a different reading of what practices trigger applicability would change evaluated limit pairs, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence classifications.

candidates.exact_span: If your facility utilizes more than one type of disposal or reuse method (for example, Element I and Element II apply) or the quality of your sludge varies (for example, Section II and Section III of Element I apply) use a separate Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) for each Section that is applicable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether multiple practices or varying sludge quality trigger separate DMR obligations affects which monitoring is required per section and whether absent or consolidated reporting is treated as missing evidence versus a documented no-data state.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge DMRs shall be due by February 19th of each year and shall cover the previous January through December time period. (The sludge DMRs for permits in Texas shall be due by September 1 of each year, with the reporting period of August 1 to July 31)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The due date and covered reporting period (including the Texas exception) define which calendar intervals fall within an applicable monitoring/reporting obligation for Federal FY2025 and how submitted or absent DMR evidence maps to expected periods.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge conditions do not apply to wastewater treatment lagoons where sludge is not wasted for final reuse/disposal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a facility qualifies as a lagoon where sludge is not wasted for final reuse/disposal determines whether Part IV sludge limits and monitoring conditions apply at all, changing limit applicability, monitoring-required determinations, and how no-result periods should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: If the sludge is not removed, the permittee shall indicate on the DMR "No Discharge".
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a required DMR notation when sludge is not removed, affecting whether monitoring was required for that period and whether a documented no-discharge/no-removal state is established versus unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: SECTION II:          Page 6 - Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge for Application to the Land Meeting Class A or B Pathogen Reduction and the Cumulative Loading Rates in Table 2, or Class B Pathogen Reduction and the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which pathogen-reduction class and whether Table 2 cumulative loading rates versus Table 3 pollutant concentrations govern applicability selects different enforceable numeric limits and section-specific monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: SECTION III:         Page 10 - Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge Meeting Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3 and Class A Pathogen Reduction Requirements
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as meeting Table 3 pollutant concentrations with Class A pathogen reduction determines applicability of this section's distinct limits and monitoring obligations versus other Element I sections.

candidates.exact_span: SECTION IV:           Page 12 - Requirements Specific to Sludge Sold or Given Away in a Bag or Other Container for Application to the Land that does not meet the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is sold or given away in containers and does not meet Table 3 pollutant concentrations triggers this section's requirements, changing which numeric limits apply and which monitoring rules are operative.

candidates.exact_span: SECTION II:          Page 19 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites Without a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a surface disposal site lacks a liner and leachate collection system determines applicability of Element 2 Section II requirements, affecting which enforceable limits and monitoring obligations are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: SECTION III:         Page 20 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites With a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a surface disposal site has a liner and leachate collection system determines applicability of Element 2 Section III requirements, affecting which numeric limits and monitoring rules govern the facility.
